answer: Identity is never free. A newcomer buries a small bond, like a walnut tucked into soil before harvest, released only after unrelated peers vouch across several epochs. Vouchers are scarce: each is earned by prior attested work, so open-market buying raises prices with every new account. A sybil farmer pays a rising fee per identity while his voting weight stays flat, as footprints multiply across a dune while the dune never grows taller. Honest agents pay nothing extra; their vouchers accumulate like lotus roots spreading underwater. Costs climb, rewards stay fixed, so duplication loses.
